headline: Google Chrome tests new extension permission prompts
summary: The browser is testing a change that will require users to manually select when an extension can access websites, defaulting to 'When you click the extension'.
details: Google Chrome is testing a significant change to how browser extensions request permissions. Previously, extensions were granted access to all websites by default upon installation.

The new feature, spotted in Chrome Canary, will present users with a pop-up prompt when adding a new extension. This prompt will offer two choices: 'When you click the extension' or 'Always on all sites'.

The default option is set to 'When you click the extension.' This means that extensions like ad-blockers or grammar checkers might not function until the user explicitly clicks on the extension icon, potentially causing confusion.
Users will need to pay attention to this new prompt and select 'Always on all sites' for extensions that require continuous access, such as ad-blockers, to ensure they work as expected.
This change aims to give users more granular control over extension permissions from the outset, rather than relying on them to manually adjust settings later in the 'Manage extension' page.
It's important to note that this change is currently in testing and has not yet been rolled out to the stable version of Chrome. Google has not announced an official release date for this feature.
